question: Vitamin D is synthesised using sunshine, by the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**skin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The skin synthesizes Vitamin D when exposed to ultraviolet B (UVB) radiation from sunlight.
 
• Vitamin D synthesis occurs when 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin absorbs UVB light, converting it into pre-vitamin D3, which is then transformed into active Vitamin D (calcitriol) in the liver and kidneys.
 
• Approximately 10–30 minutes of sun exposure, a few times a week, is sufficient for most people to produce adequate Vitamin D levels, depending on skin type and geographical location.
 
• The process is influenced by factors such as time of day, season, latitude, skin pigmentation, and sunscreen usage.
 
• Vitamin D plays a crucial role in calcium absorption, bone health, immune function, and overall well-being.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **7-dehydrocholesterol:** A precursor molecule found in the skin that absorbs UVB radiation to initiate Vitamin D synthesis.
 
• **Calcitriol (Active Vitamin D):** The biologically active form of Vitamin D, which is essential for maintaining calcium and phosphate homeostasis in the body.
 
• **Deficiency Risks:** Lack of sufficient sunlight exposure or dietary intake can lead to Vitamin D deficiency, causing rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.
 
• **Dietary Sources:** While sunlight is the primary source, Vitamin D can also be obtained from foods like fatty fish, egg yolks, fortified dairy products, and supplements.
 
• **UVB Radiation:** A type of ultraviolet light with wavelengths between 280–315 nm, critical for Vitamin D production but also associated with the risk of skin damage and cancer if overexposed.
